description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model evaluated under varying levels of initial confidence. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear scale from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major ticks every 0.2 units. The “Final Accuracy” (blue line with circle markers and solid line) remains consistently high across all confidence levels, starting at approximately 0.93 at 0.86 confidence and peaking near 1.0 at 0.97–0.99 confidence before slightly declining to 0.98 at 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers and dashed line) begins at approximately 0.65 at 0.86 confidence, rises gradually to a peak of about 0.92 at 0.97 confidence, then drops to 0.77 at 1.00 confidence. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange line with diamond markers and dash-dotted line) starts at approximately 0.28 at 0.86 confidence, declines to a minimum of about 0.05 near 0.94–0.95 confidence, then rises again to 0.20 at 1.00 confidence. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements, with larger error margins observed for Δ Accuracy and Initial Accuracy compared to Final Accuracy.
